title: Warm-start credit vesting + security-questionnaire gated upgrade (conversion anchoring experiment)
creator: Sofia Alvarez
description: Goal: improve trial-to-paid conversion and early product activation by testing two related mechanics: (1) warm-start credit vesting (daily drip) to encourage repeat usage, and (2) an SQ-gated credit unlock that anchors enterprise buyers to complete the security questionnaire and start contract conversations. This ticket scopes the experiment variants, instrumentation, rollout plan, stakeholder approvals, and success metrics.
hypothesis: H1: Users who receive a warm-start vesting schedule (smaller immediate credit + daily drip over 30 days) will have higher D7 and D14 active session rates and higher conversion to paid within 30 days versus a single large upfront credit with the same nominal value. H2: Offering a larger credit pool that unlocks only after completing the security questionnaire will increase SQ completion rate and accelerate enterprise conversion conversations without significantly harming self-serve conversion velocity.
success_metrics: Primary: trial -> paid conversion within 30 days (uplift vs control). Secondary: D1/D7/D14 active sessions, number of API calls (tokens consumed) in trial, SQ completion rate, demo/enterprise lead creation (CRM), gross credit consumption rate. Safety: no >10% drop in overall sign-up conversion or large spike in fraud/abuse signals.
variants: Control: current baseline (single upfront credit 5k tokens, 30-day expiry). Variant A (Vesting): 1,200 immediate + 60 tokens/day drip for 30 days (total ~3k). Variant B (Gated-SQ): 600 immediate + 2,400 locked until SQ completion or sales opt-in (max 30 days). Variant C (Anchored-commit): 3,000 credits unlocked immediately if user opts into a 3-month reserved discount (commitment anchor), otherwise fall back to Control.
rollout_plan: Staged rollout: internal QA -> 1% of new sign-ups (7 days) -> 5% (14 days) -> 25% (21 days) -> 100% if no regressions. Early kill criteria: >10% reduction in onboarding activation (first API call within 24h), >15% increase in fraud signals, or >5% drop in sign-up conversion. Ramp control: feature-flagged variant assignment managed in Growth experimentation service. Duration: 6 weeks from full ramp to primary analysis.
data_and_instrumentation: Events to instrument: 'credit_awarded' (variant, amount, unlock_policy), 'credit_drip' (amount, day), 'sq_completed', 'upgrade_clicked', 'upgrade_converted', 'api_call', 'signup'. Required dashboard queries: cohort by variant -> D1/D7/D14 activation, token consumption curves, SQ funnel. Data owners: Data Eng (Ana Ribeiro), Growth Analytics (Liam O'Connor). Dashboard prototype: https://dash.redwood.com/d/experiment/warm-start-72109 (placeholder). BI tickets: ENG-4987 (credit accounting event schema), ENG-5012 (SQ webhook), DATA-1221 (experiment dashboard)
engineering_changes: Backend: add 'vesting' credit policy and locked-credit flag, migration to credit ledger (idempotent). Console: new UX for gated message and SQ CTA, dropdown for commitment anchor. PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/8342 (backend credit logic), https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/921 (UX and messaging). Require load testing on Dedicated path for worst-case eager consumption.
legal_and_security_considerations: Security needs to sign off on the SQ gating messaging and any opt-in contract flow. Legal to review language for commitment anchor (discount + credits). Security review required: true. Contacts: Legal - Priya Nair, Security - Marcus Lee. Checklist: no PII in credit events, SQ completion must record consent and timestamp, KMS audit on any customer contract terms.
qa_acceptance_criteria: 1) Variant assignment stable and logged. 2) Credit ledger reconciles exactly across award and consumption events for n=500 test users. 3) Console messaging shows correct locked state and SQ CTA. 4) SQ webhook triggers credit unlock within SLA (60s). 5) No regressions in signup or token billing metrics in smoke tests.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: large credits abused by automated scrapers -> mitigation: rate-limit heavy consumers, require phone/email verification for high-volume unlocks, monitor fraud signals. Risk: gating SQ slows self-serve growth -> mitigation: keep a baseline immediate credit so self-serve funnel remains healthy; A/B test only subset. Risk: accounting edge cases -> mitigation: reconcile workflows and playbook for manual adjustments.
follow_up_tasks: 1) Prepare A/B config in experimentation service (Growth Eng). 2) Add experiment-specific BI slices and alerts. 3) Legal sign-off on commitment wording. 4) Run internal canary with Redwood employees (two-week pilot). 5) Prepare sales playbook for leads generated by SQ completion.
